title: Cyprus Avenue with Stephen Rea at Royal Court - review
transcript: cypress Avenue by David Ireland is a black comedy about a Belfast loyalist that's someone usually a Protestant who wants Northern Ireland to remain part of the United Kingdom he's done something bad and he's seeing a psychiatrist played by Ron key Attica lujo we learn that he's a bigoted man in fear of losing his identity as British in a series of flashbacks he's seen meeting his granddaughter for the first time and believing that she's Jerry Adams the president of shin Thane the political wing of the IRA from then on it's a rollercoaster ride as he vacillates between his love for his family and its newest member and his prejudice against Jerry Adams and all things Irish Catholic there are two reasons you need to watch this David Ireland's hilarious script and Steven Rae's delivery of it the latter has a face for which the expression hangdog could have been invented and Eric's sadness and confusion and frustration are all there in that face his hunched posture suggests the weight of Irish history and if like me you think of Steven rare as an actor who exudes languid --mess well think again because the best moment in this play is a monologue akin to stand-up comedy where Eric races back and forth ranting and raving about Irishness well it had be rolling around on my sofa and that alone is worth the ticket price if you are paying keep watching for more about Cyprus Avenue filmed live at the Royal Court we first meet Eric played by Steven Rae on a bare stage with the audience on two sides Travis style a nice touch by designer Lizzie clack and I thought to suggest the Protestant loyalist Catholic Republican divide and the square of the stage is also in a sense the inside of Eric's closed mind with characters appearing and disappearing as he thinks about them Stephen rare is supported by some precision directing from Vicki Featherstone where every move seems to mean something and some fine actors Amy Malloy is his daughter Julie who loves her dad but is offended by him an internal conflict that she really makes you feel she represents hope a younger generation who've grown up with peace and are no longer twisted by sectarian prejudice under Irvine is Eric's firm but caring wife and chris corrigan steals his scenes as a loyalist terrorists whose lust for violence is tempered by philosophical thoughts and guided by the finest minds of the Ulster Volunteer Force David Ireland's script sparks and fizzes with laughs at the expense of Eric's shockingly warped logic and bizarre prejudices he he talks of exotic Catholic hairdos direct from the salons of the Vatican as an examination of how loss of identity can lead to bigotry can lead to psychotic behavior this play works well but the ending which I won't spoil for you left me feeling that the player had gone too far in wanting to shock it draws comparison with Martin McDonough's the lieutenant of Inishmore which with all due respect to the unquestionable quality of David Islands writing is a better thought through play and what we miss in this filmed version is the way as a member of the theatre audience you would be looking up at the actors and always seeing an opposing audience in the background as well as the whole stage and its boundaries and while we gain from extreme close-ups of Steven Rae's magnificently craggy face we lose quite a bit of the time the stage actors are - suggesting emotion and meaning through their whole body and of course the film director chooses what you look at and while I accept that Steven Rae is riveting there were times when I wished as in some football coverage that I could switch to a different camera looking into another actors reaction and the addition of some location filming in Belfast is a mistake it didn't add anything for me and merely broke the tension of the intimate and closed stage setting so I found the play flawed but the production is terrific and Steven Rae gives what must be the performance of a lifetime I give cypress Avenue for stars but you can see it for yourself so what do you think please watch it and then scroll down and comment and if you found this review interesting or useful please
